outlook.statement: The logistics industry is undergoing a structural transformation driven by digitisation, technology adoption, data-led decision-making, improved road infrastructure, integrated supply chains and increasing emphasis on efficiency and sustainability. OBCL intends to remain responsive to these changes and continuously evolve its capabilities to meet the changing requirements of its customers.
Priorities for the years ahead will remain centred on customer centricity, operational excellence, prudent financial management, technology adoption and sustainable expansion.

Focus is not merely on growth in scale, but on creating quality and sustainable growth. Determined to strengthen operational foundations, improve profitability, enhance customer relationships and create long-term value for all stakeholders.

Global logistics market valued between USD 4.3 trillion and USD 12.7 trillion in 2026 with projected CAGR 3.7% to 10.1%. Indian logistics market valued at approximately USD 243.8 billion in 2025 with sustained growth expected. India's logistics costs estimated at 13-14% of GDP, higher than 8-10% in developed economies. Government initiatives like National Logistics Policy and PM Gati Shakti expected to improve supply chain efficiency and reduce logistics costs.

The Board is optimistic about long-term growth in the transport sector and is confident in the Company's potential to capitalize on emerging opportunities. Management remains committed to improving profitability and ensuring sustainable growth.

OBCL is exploring opportunities in untapped sectors of the transport industry. A new software platform is under development to onboard over 10,000 commercial transport vehicles, expected to significantly boost operations and competitiveness.

Structural inefficiencies in Indian logistics: sub-optimal modal mix, fragmented regulatory frameworks, gaps in warehousing and multimodal connectivity, shortage of skilled manpower, inadequate intermodal and last-mile connectivity
Highly fragmented and competitive unorganized goods transportation industry in India
Need for Integrated Logistics Infrastructure - highly unorganised sector with small independent operators leading to inefficient resource use, limited standardisation and poor coordination
Impact of Volatile Fuel Prices on Logistics - fuel makes up major part of transportation costs; global price changes affect domestic diesel costs and industry margins
Addressing Truck Driver Shortage - profession appears unattractive due to safety concerns, tough working conditions, irregular hours and extended time away from home
Enhancing Last-Mile Delivery Efficiency - challenges include limited manpower, inadequate road infrastructure, traffic congestion, inaccurate address mapping and weather-related disruptions
Geopolitical and Socio-Political Risks - war, terrorist attacks, civil unrest or communal disturbances could impact financial markets and equity share price
Regulatory and Legal Uncertainties - changes in laws, regulations or tax policies may increase compliance burdens, operational costs or liabilities
